title: Consumption Contract Orchestration Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Playbook describing the product design, requirements, rollout, pricing implications, and release notes for the Consumption Contract Orchestration capability — a control plane that codifies per-customer consumption contracts, fidelity tiers, and entitlements and automates enforcement and billing reconciliation across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines the scope, product requirements, design constraints, rollout plan, pricing considerations, and release artifacts for the Consumption Contract Orchestration (CCO) initiative. CCO provides a unified contract engine that maps customer entitlements (SLOs, fidelity tiers, capacity commitments, burst allowances) to runtime routing, telemetry tagging, billing hooks, and fallback policies. The goal is to make consumption guarantees auditable, enforceable, and reconcilable across hosted, dedicated and private deployments.

Why this capability:
- Reduce manual contract-translation work between Sales, Legal and Engineering.
- Ensure runtime behavior (fallbacks, throttles, priority shaping) matches negotiated commercial terms.
- Provide deterministic billing and reconciliations for hybrid deployments where enforcement surface differs.
- Enable product experimentation: entitlement-based A/B and canary configurations without bespoke infra changes.

Goals (success metrics):
1) Reduce time-to-turnup for SLA-entitlement customers from signed contract to production enforcement to < 7 business days.
2) Zero customer-facing mismatches between contracted SLOs and observed SLO breaches attributable to configuration drift in 95% of cases.
3) Provide a reconciliation delta < 0.5% between runtime-metered consumption and invoiced consumption for customers with entitlements.
4) Support fidelity tiers and burst crediting for 100% of new Dedicated customer signups in first 6 months after GA.

High-level product scope:
- Contract model language (JSON schema) to express: per-route SLO weights, fidelity tiers, burst credit pools, preemptible capacity allowances, and observability retention levels.
- Orchestration service to compile contracts into runtime routing rules, quota policies, and billing hooks.
- Developer console UI and CLI for preview, validation, and staged activation.
- Integration points: Billing system (reconciliation webhook), Runtime routing API (policy push), Console dashboards (entitlement view), Audit logging (immutable contract events).

Non-goals:
- Not a full legal contract authoring tool (Legal still issues executed master agreements).
- Does not replace low-level per-model execution optimizations (that remains runtime domain).

Requirements (minimum viable):
- RQ-001: Contract Schema - Provide a stable JSON schema v1.0 that expresses: customer_id, contract_id, effective_dates, routes (pattern), slo_targets (p99 latency ms, availability pct), fidelity_tier (enum), burst_pool (tokens), preemptible_percent, metering_tags.
- RQ-002: Validation - Syntactic and semantic validation with helpful error messages surfaced in Console and CLI.
- RQ-003: Compile & Push - Atomic compilation to runtime policies with an idempotent push API and per-deployment target (hosted/dedicated/private).
- RQ-004: Audit log - Every contract change emits an immutable audit event with user, timestamp, diff, and rollout plan id.
- RQ-005: Preview mode - Dry-run simulation that shows expected routing decisions for a supplied traffic sample.
- RQ-006: Billing Hooks - Reconciliation output file (NDJSON) compatible with existing billing ingestion with fields: contract_id, timestamp_bucket, tokens_consumed, fidelity_credit_used, fallback_count.
- RQ-007: Entitlement Mappings UX - Console view that maps commercial line-items to contract fields and highlights gaps.

Design considerations and constraints:
- Backwards compatibility: runtime must accept both CCO-managed policies and legacy per-tenant hand-configured routes during migration; priority: no customer-impacting behavior change during staged activation.
- Deterministic policy ordering: explicit precedence rules documented (contract-level > route-level > global defaults).
- Latency impact: push operations should be ultimately consistent across fleet; runtime must honor last-applied timestamp and support incremental deltas to avoid brief configuration spikes.
- Security: contract documents are sensitive. Encrypt contract storage at rest (KMS) and restrict UI access via RBAC.

Compile & Runtime contract mapping (text table):
| Contract field | Runtime artifact | Notes |
| contract_id | policy_id | 1:1 mapping; used in audit traces |
| routes.pattern | routing_rule | supports glob and regex; prefer prefix match for perf |
| slo_targets.p99_ms | latency_weight | used by adaptive scheduler to shape priority |
| fidelity_tier | model_variant_selector | resolves to allowed model variants and quantization profiles |
| burst_pool.tokens | burst_credit_account | reconciles to metering connector every minute |

Rollout plan (recommended):
1) Phase 0 - Internal dogfood (2 weeks): onboard 1 internal product team, exercise contract lifecycle flows, validate reconciliation hooks.
2) Phase 1 - Beta (4–6 weeks): recruit 3 early-adopter customers (mix of hosted + dedicated) for live traffic trials; provide dedicated SRE support window.
3) Phase 2 - Opt-in GA (8 weeks): open to self-serve for customers with entitlements; add billing reconciliation certification.
4) Phase 3 - Enforced GA (target): default enforcement for new enterprise contracts.

Operational runbook (abridged):
- On contract push failure: rollback using rollout plan id; alert on-call SRE; notify contract owner.
- On reconciliation delta > 1% for any customer: create incident, enumerate diff, pause new activations until manual signoff.
- If policy push causes routing anomalies: revert last policy push and engage the compile-service owner.

Pricing & commercial considerations:
- Entitlement packaging: offer CCO as an included capability for Enterprise tiers; charge an add-on for self-managed Private deployments where we provide orchestration connectors.
- Burst credits accounting: Introduce a fractional credit unit (0.001 credit) to enable fine-grained metering of microbursts; map to billing buckets with hourly aggregation.
- Migration credits: Provide a migration credit pool for the first billing period for early-adopter customers to offset initial reconciliation small deltas.
- Legal hooks: require a short contract amendment template that references CCO policy IDs to create an auditable link between the commercial contract and runtime policy.

Console UX & APIs (developer experience):
- Console views: Contract list, Contract diff viewer, Simulation preview, Entitlement-to-invoice preview.
- CLI: cco validate <file.json>, cco preview <file.json> --sample-traffic sample.ndjson, cco push <file.json> --target=dedicated --staged-rollout=10%.
- API: POST /v1/cco/contracts (returns rollout_plan_id), GET /v1/cco/contracts/{id}/preview, POST /v1/cco/compile/push

Acceptance criteria (product):
- All RQ-* items implemented and tested.
- End-to-end dogfood with at least one Dedicated and one Hosted tenant with simulated and real traffic.
- Billing ingestion successfully reconciles sample NDJSON outputs for 3 billing cycles without manual adjustment.
- Console UX validated by at least 5 customers in beta with NPS >= 8 for contract UX flows.

Compatibility matrix (text):
- Hosted: full support (policy push + billing hooks).
- Dedicated: full support (policy push + billing hooks) for Dedicated clusters running runtime v3.2+.
- Private (on-prem): partial support — CCO provides policy bundle and reconciliation payloads; customer must install local connector (open-source agent) for push and audit ingestion.

Telemetry and observability requirements:
- Emit policy_apply.success and policy_apply.failure metrics with tags: contract_id, target_deployment, user_id.
- Traces: compile -> push -> runtime_apply spans preserved with rollout_plan_id.
- Dashboards: Per-contract SLO attainment, credit burn rate, fallback rate, reconciliation delta.

Security and compliance notes:
- Contract storage: encrypted with customer-key-support for Private deployments.
- Audit retention: 24 months by default; configurable per-contract during commercial negotiation.
- Data residency: allow contract storage region pinning when requested by customer.

Open questions (to resolve prior to GA):
- Q1: How granular should legal amendment linking be (single clause per contract or per route)? Recommendation: per-contract policy IDs with optional route-level clause for high-risk customers.
- Q2: SLA enforcement granularity for mixed-route contracts. Recommendation: allow per-route SLOs but surface an aggregated contract-level SLO in the console and invoices.

Roadmap milestones (quarterly coarse plan):
- Q1 2027: GA for Hosted + Dedicated; billing connectors certified.
- Q2 2027: Private connector release and RBAC console refinements.
- Q3 2027: Advanced fidelity negotiation API and canary-based staged activations.
- Q4 2027: Auto-reconciliation suggestions and billing-exception automation.

Release notes (initial 0.9 beta release):
- Feature: Contract JSON schema v1.0 and validation service.
- Feature: Compile service and idempotent push API (supports prefix-based route matching).
- Feature: Console contract diff viewer and preview mode (sample traffic replay).
- Integration: Billing NDJSON reconciliation schema and ingestion demo.
- Known limitations: Private connector not yet available; reconciliation delta reporting reports hourly buckets (future: minute-level).

Appendix A — Example contract snippet (JSON, trimmed):
{
  "customer_id": "cust-1034",
  "contract_id": "C-2026-451",
  "effective_from": "2027-01-01",
  "routes": [
    {"pattern": "/v1/chat/*", "slo_targets": {"p99_ms": 250, "availability_pct": 99.9}, "fidelity_tier": "standard"}
  ],
  "burst_pool": {"tokens": 100000}
}
